title: A Key Left Out
summary: A web server serves a folder it shouldn't, and in it is a private SSH key. The key lets you in without a password; a writable service script lets you up.
story: Marigold Media (made up) runs web01 on 10.10.4.0/24. You start on scout. Somewhere on the web server is a backup folder that was never meant to be public.
goal: Capture the user flag in the webadmin home folder and the root flag in /root.
skills: web folder listings, SSH private keys, file permissions, writable root cron script

hints.text: Scan 10.10.4.30, fetch its pages, and look for a folder listing. webscan http://10.10.4.30/ tries common folder names.
The /backup/ folder lists its files. One is id_rsa, an SSH private key. Save it, make it private (chmod 600), and use it: ssh -i id_rsa webadmin@10.10.4.30
As webadmin, look at what root runs on a timer (ls -l /etc/cron.d, then the script it names). If the script is writable, add a line that copies /root/flag.txt somewhere readable and wait a minute.
